reviews.review:
I’m avoiding any kind of real spoilers in this review, for those interested. I’m also going to compare this game to EDF 4.1 quite a bit. If you haven’t played it and you’re looking at EDF 5, you might want to start there.

I can’t give EDF 5 the same amazing, 10/10 rating I would give EDF 4.1. Its hard to pin down exactly why for, but there are a couple things I will cover in my review. If you played it already and want the quick version, its still a great game and if you liked 4.1 you will like 5. Its vaguely less grindy and has a lot of QoL improvements, the classes are a little more varied and weapon balance is much better overall (nearly everything is viable) but the mission and enemy variety is weaker. Most of what I talk about in this review are my complaints, not the good aspects of the game. Its still a great game, and there is basically nothing else like it right now.

It also hasn't crashed or had any technical problems at all for me, which is far more than I can say for 4.1.

BASICS:

To start with, there are a couple obvious changes that are contentious, and are listed in most other reviews if you want to read more. First, difficulties past hard are locked until you beat the previous one. Technically, very hard and inferno are supposed to require high level gear to complete, but this is still pretty much directly a step back as skilled groups (and wing divers) can do them early. Second, weapons have levels now, in which they gain stats when you pick up duplicates of the same weapon. What they gain seems random, but there is some kind of level limit involved. E.G, you can’t max a weapon on the minimum level mission you picked it up on. I don’t feel very strongly about either of these changes, so I won’t say much. I don’t think the leveled weapons are nearly as bad as others do though.

LEVELS AND PROGRESSION:

EDF 4.1 had a vague sense of difficulty, story, and mission progression through the missions. Scenarios tended to get harder, enemies became more varied, and a story and general sense of doom and foreboding increased. This is not the case in EDF 5. 

To begin, the difficulty in EDF 5 is very far from linear. Many missions are nothing new, and are often not that hard as a result. On the other hand, a couple difficulty spikes are absolutely brutal and can be quite hard even on normal if you don’t have the gear or a good understanding of what strategy or weapons the enemies require to defeat. Honestly, this is isn’t a HUGE problem by itself, but it leads right into my next complaint.

ENEMY AND MISSION VARIETY:

This section in general holds most of my complaints. Way too many of the missions feel suspiciously similar, to the point of seeming like filler. The amazing commentary by NPCs is mostly absent in these, and the enemies and maps are nothing new. This isn’t to say there aren’t a ton of great missions, in fact there are probably MORE of those amazing, memorable missions in 5 than 4.1, but that definitely comes down to opinion. I’m really not sure why this happened. They’ve shown they’re perfectly capable of making great missions with little commentary by plot characters even in 4.1, so this really disappointed me.

I want to reiterate here, even the enemy variety is worse. Even returning enemies like the jumping spiders are much more homogenized. Instead of being a more unique and tailored enemy, they are just “Stronger Bug Number 3.” They still have the same jank ass web attack, but now do slightly less damage and have much more health. They’re also slower and can’t jump as far. The health change is much more noticeable than I’m making it sound, and I don’t like it. Every time I see spiders I just sigh because they’re essentially a bigger, nastier ant now. 

The other problem is a much stronger enemy I wont name for spoilers that is used way, WAY too much throughout the game. Its responsible for many of the filler missions that tend to play out exactly the same. While the enemy itself is very interactive, the most effective strategy for beating them is exactly the same, every single time, every single mission, for basically every class. 

Finally, missions with many combinations of enemies on the field are much rarer than 4.1, which also lends to the roller-coaster of difficulty I mentioned. Missions with only one enemy type are easier than missions with mixed enemies, this is simply a fact. While these missions were also present in 4.1, there are far too many of them in 5. 

VOICE ACTING AND STORY:

Lets just get this out of the way, the voice lines… are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible.

But let me clarify, the voice acting itself is quite good, its on par with 4.1. The writing on the other hand is god awful. Its bad, and the iconic EDF song is completely irredeemable compared to 4.1. The infantry lines are all pretty good, but they don’t make up for everything else. The announcer/comms is also incredibly boring compared to 4.1, and far less animated. There’s not much else to say, its really bad.

CLASSES AND WEAPONS:

I’m happy to say the class and weapon variety seems to be much better across the board. Nearly every type of weapon is viable, which is a huge improvement over 4.1. Rangers can sprint and have a vehicle slot, air raiders have some of their air strikes converted to a short cooldown rather than a point cost (the quick ones like a single cannon shell), and fencers feel a bit less janky. The controls generally feel better overall. Its hard to quantify. Also, when you lose a mission you now keep half the armor and weapons you picked up (on hard). 

Some vehicles are quite expensive point wise, but often start with a bonus for the first one you drop. As vehicles level with the new weapon leveling system, they often cost less points as a benefit to this. This is probably the only time I really dislike the leveling system, as having a vehicle be more expensive can make it exponentially worse than a stat change.
My other major complaint here, is that vehicles seem to be somewhat worse compared to normal weapons than they were in 4.1. Their damage often lags majorly behind other classes weapons, and given the new cooldown based airstrikes, I think Sandlot wanted to move in a direction where vehicles are no longer the “weapon” of air raiders, which I really hate. For transparencies sake, air raider is my favorite class, and seeing it take this hit really makes me angry. Vehicles were tricky to use due to being easy targets for high DPS bugs, but were a very unique playstyle. Now they don’t seem to have the damage to compensate. They’re still viable, but I felt the change.

All and all, its still a great game but I was hoping it would live up to 4.1 and I can’t decide if it does right now. Hopefully they can release some DLC missions with good variety like the 4.1 mission packs contain.

El día de hoy venimos a hablar de un juego que tiene un gran recorrido, uno que tuvo un gran inicio en oriente siendo todo un éxito en la PlayStation 2. Yéndonos muy atrás, por allá del año 2003, el juego vería su primer entrada en la saga, pasando por una serie de spin-offs, y llegando a occidente en 2007 en la consola Xbox 360. Nosotros hemos probado la entrega de 2019, Earth Defence Force 5 en PC, aunque también está disponible para PlayStation 4.

Earth Defence Force se enfoca en todas sus entregas sobre un mismo arco narrativo: la tierra se ve atacada por un grupo de monstruos gigantes que llegan en incontables cantidades; salen de la nada y hacen que todos los ejércitos del mundo se unan para eliminarlos de una vez por todas. Por más que al jugarlo tenemos claro que la narrativa no es su fuerte, no deja de tener destellos muy fugaces en lo que a la misma se refiere (meramente cosillas chistosas).

Y bueno, en esta quinta entrada, el tema de la trama no es la excepción. EDF 5 nos pone la piel de un civil que entra a un búnker subterráneo de la armada, pero, en el momento que le dan un tour de bienvenida, los monstruos hacen su entrada y atacan el lugar. Allí, inicia nuestro camino en pos de la liberación mundial de la amenaza alienígena.

Al ir escapando, uno de los capitanes de pelotón nos ayuda a salir, pero al ver su grupo mermado, no le queda otra opción que darnos un arma. En ese momento, es cuando el capitán se da cuenta que somos una máquina de matar y sencillamente nos mete en su cuadrilla, nos contrata al mero descaro.

Más adelante, vamos teniendo el chance de acceder a nuevos tipos de soldados. En general, hay cuatro tipos de guerreros: el Ranger, el Wing Diver, el Air Raider y el Fencer. El Ranger tiene la posibilidad de equiparse con armamento muy poderoso, pero se ve limitado en su movilidad al andar a pie (aunque puede llamar vehículos). El Wing Diver, tal como lo dice su nombre, puede volar, incluso, tiene acceso a equipamiento alienígena, pero es bastante débil (vitalidad) con relación al Ranger. Por otro lado tenemos al Air Raider es un personaje de apoyo, y tiene la posibilidad de poner sentry guns por el mapeado. Para finalizar, el Fencer, es un tanque que lleva consigo un exo-esqueleto muy poderoso, escudos, y es fuerte en el cuerpo a cuerpo, pero es realmente lento.

El juego es un shooter bastante arcade -en tercera persona. Es muy fiel a su estilo y aunque la receta de jugabilidad no cambia nunca, siempre hallan la manera de hacerlo muy adictivo. En EDF 5 tenemos más de lo mismo, pero se hace un placer enorme matar insectos de escalas irreales, mechas gigantes, ranas cyborg, y muchos otros enemigos fantásticos.

Este título se desarrolla mediante misiones, las cuales nos hacen avanzar en la trama de ‘salvar al mundo’. Cada una de ellas nos invita a avanzar por entre niveles donde toparemos con centenares de enemigos en pantalla; casi siempre nos ponen a correr por calles o corredores, y muy pocas son de estilo defender la zona. A nuestra disposición contamos con dos armas principales, las cuales varían según el personaje que elegimos, pero que tienen siempre la misma función: irnos abriendo paso por la gran cantidad de atacantes gigantes.

El disparar es super arcade, en tercera persona, y las armas tienen un recoil inexistente. Otras mecánicas involucran saltar y girar en el suelo para evitar ataques de los monstruos. El resultado y el desarrollo de dicho cometido es simplemente satisfactorio. Incluso con sus visuales de PlayStation 2, Earth Defence Force 5 es lo suficientemente bueno como para darnos mucha diversión. Por si fuera poco, tenemos un modo local para dos jugadores que hace que todo lo bueno que hay en el juego se multiplique por dos, en caso de tener un amigo en casa. Por si eso no fuese suficiente, es posible entrar a partidas online con hasta otros tres amigos, y así, liberar al mundo del peligro entre cuatro personas. A la hora de jugar partidas online, hacer un buen uso de cada uno de los personajes es vital para no sucumbir ante el embate de los alienígenas en las modalidades de alta dificultad.

Yo no hallo algo en lo qué quejarme del título, aunque sí puedo decir que noté algunos bajones de FPS en ciertas partes donde habían muchas explosiones, cuando los tanques iban detrás de nuestro pelotón haciendo cobertura. Por demás, no vi algún problema técnico. Los trabajos en voces resultan divertidos, ni siquiera podemos tomarlos en serio debido al enfoque del juego, pero digamos, no son malos, me hicieron reír y también dan un poco de inmersión al ambiente pues vas oyendo como los generales dan órdenes al contingente. El sonido de los efectos especiales pues, está entre malo y regular, pero tampoco estamos jugando Battlefield V.

Con una gran simpleza en sus mecánicas y jugabilidad, hallamos en Earth Defence Force 5 un título que nos hará pasar un gran rato. Su campaña es bastante larga, y entre casi un centenar de misiones tendremos bastante variedad para no sentir todo muy repetitivo. Lo bueno es que las partidas multijugador le dan una rejugabilidad todavía mayor, lo que además aumenta mucho el factor diversión a la hora de tirarnos a salvar al planeta.

De momento EDF 5 cuenta con notas muy positivas en la tienda de Steam, de entre más de 1300 valoraciones de usuarios de la plataforma. El juego tiene un precio de $50 USD.
I will forever buy any new EDF game. I always keep coming back to grind a bit more. And I always get something new to play with.
